questions.question: For the reaction 2N2O5(g) → 4NO2(g) + O2(g), the rate of disappearance of N2O5 at an instant is 0.02 mol L^-1 s^-1. Find the rates of formation of NO2 and of O2 at that instant.

For a reaction A + B → products, doubling [A] at constant [B] doubles the initial rate, while doubling [B] at constant [A] makes the initial rate four times larger. Write the rate law, give the overall order, and state the units of the rate constant.

The reaction 2H2(g) + 2NO(g) → N2(g) + 2H2O(g) follows this mechanism: 2NO(g) ⇌ N2O2(g) (fast equilibrium, k1 and k-1); N2O2(g) + H2(g) → N2O(g) + H2O(g) (slow, k2); N2O(g) + H2(g) → N2(g) + H2O(g) (fast, k3). What is the order of the reaction?
A first order reaction is 40% complete in 50 minutes. Calculate its rate constant and the time it takes to be 80% complete. (log 2 = 0.301, log 3 = 0.477, log 5 = 0.699)

For the first order reaction 2N2O5(g) → 4NO2(g) + O2(g) (A) the concentration of the reactant decreases exponentially with time. (B) the half-life of the reaction decreases with increasing temperature. (C) the half-life of the reaction depends on the initial concentration of the reactant. (D) the reaction proceeds to 99.6% completion in eight half-life durations.
If the half-life of a first order reaction is 6.93 minutes, how many minutes are required for 99% of the reaction to be completed? (Given: log 2 = 0.3010)

The rate of a first order reaction is 0.04 mol L^-1 s^-1 at 10 minutes and 0.03 mol L^-1 s^-1 at 20 minutes after initiation. What is the half-life of the reaction in minutes? (Given: log 2 = 0.3010, log 3 = 0.4771)
The rate constant of a reaction is 2.0 × 10^-2 s^-1 at 300 K and 8.0 × 10^-2 s^-1 at 320 K. Calculate the activation energy of the reaction. (R = 8.314 J K^-1 mol^-1, log 4 = 0.602)

For a reversible reaction A ⇌ B, ΔH of the forward reaction is 20 kJ mol^-1 and the activation energy of the uncatalysed forward reaction is 300 kJ mol^-1. When the reaction is catalysed, keeping the reactant concentration the same, the rate of the catalysed forward reaction at 27 °C equals that of the uncatalysed reaction at 327 °C. What is the activation energy, in kJ mol^-1, of the catalysed backward reaction?

According to the collision theory of bimolecular gaseous reactions, why does only a small fraction of collisions between reactant molecules lead to products? Explain the roles of the threshold energy, proper orientation and the steric factor P in the rate expression.
